name: Eli Aranda
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember collecting hats for the school costume cupboard.” People around the bank steps know Eli by a small Sunday habit. Eli takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I collected the clippings for a school play and got ten people telling me about their first haircuts.
appearance: Eli has one cheek that creases before the other. Look for auburn hair cut square at the nape. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a soft blue checked shirt with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. In conversation Eli presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Eli reads little signals of discomfort very accurately and has an unfortunate habit of overruling people for their own good. The friends who say stop are the ones Eli trusts most.
agenda: To complete the school play's costume collection.
family: Finn Ross is Eli’s half-sibling. Eli chooses the familiar route. Finn can stop the walk at any corner. Walking side by side makes it easier to disagree without turning each disagreement into a contest. Asked about *First shift back*, Finn says, “I covered for the absent colleague and finally felt good at my job.”
connections: Pat Fraser. A conversation heard through the wall finds its way back into a school costume story.

reactions.situation: A customer uses the free haircut to talk
reactions.response: Eli lets the visitor say whether they would like a trim as well as a talk.

reactions.situation: The last bus leaves while an elderly stranger is still crossing toward it
reactions.response: Eli waits at the lit stop with them and checks whether the next service is one they can actually board.
